summary: A Windows 11 VM that has never seen this project, snapshotted clean, so E2, E3 and E10 can ask whether a stranger can install the app

coordination.notes: Nothing was installed on the host for this. VirtualBox 7.0.18 was already present. The ISO lives outside the repository at C:/Users/Admin/dev/_scratch/vm/win11-ltsc-eval.iso, not in any git tree. The VM has no shared folders and clipboard and drag-and-drop are disabled, so it cannot reach the host tree another session might be working in.

checks: VM drc-clean-win11 exists, UUID d2f33cb1-de66-4385-b131-e0cccd85c80b, VMState=poweroff
snapshot 'clean' exists, UUID f3d11570-c6a9-46d2-99c1-77e300027040, taken powered off with the install ISO detached

the ISO is Microsoft's own: go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=2289029 redirects to software-static.download.prss.microsoft.com, and the downloaded file is 5,112,850,432 bytes, exactly the Content-Length the server returned

build 26100.1742 from two independent sources: VirtualBox's own inspection of the ISO before install (detectedOSVersion = 10.0.26100.1742) and the booted desktop's watermark (Build 26100.ge_release.240331-1435)
`ver` was NOT run in the guest - VBoxManage guestcontrol returned 'the guest execution service is not ready (yet)' twice. docs/verification/vm.md says so rather than implying an in-guest reading.
the booted desktop was looked at, not inferred: a screenshot shows a logged-in Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC Evaluation desktop

the install appeared to be running for about twenty-five minutes and had done nothing - it was parked on 'Press any key to boot from CD or DVD' and had fallen through to 'No bootable option or device was found'. VMState="running" was true and meaningless. Caught by screenshotting rather than trusting the state field, which is the whole of section 1 of CLAUDE.md in one instance.

a second trap from the fix: hammering Enter past the boot prompt then lands on Windows Setup's Cancel button and raises 'Are you sure you want to quit?', blocking the install behind a modal. Esc did not dismiss it; the accelerator 'n' did. Both recorded in the doc.
